title_en: Intermediate English - 18 - How has your life changed in the last five years?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Preah. I am from Belize and I am an ESL teacher. Belize is in Central America. It is actually the only English speaking country in Central America. And my question was how has your life changed in the last five years?

And I'm glad I got this question because two days ago I was thinking about this exact same thing. I am 21 years old, will be 22 in November. So five years ago I was actually graduating high school. Yes, I am a 2017 graduate and since then I have traveled. I have a 2-year-old daughter. I have lived in three different and three different locations in my country. So I've moved around a bit and I am now a teacher myself. So in five years I would say a lot has happened. I am going to school, I'm about to graduate university in one year, and I have met thousands and thousands of people that are from all around the world have a lot of knowledge from traveling experiences that I never would've had if I had just stayed in my hometown. So those are the different changes.

title_en: What language would you like to learn?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Juan Cruz. I'm from Argentina. My question is, what language would you like to learn?

Well, I would like to learn Italian. I'm currently starting to learn the language because my family is Italian descent, which is very common in Argentina. And I think learning this language would help me reconnect and understand where I'm from, and I would love to one day be able to go back to Italy knowing the language and being able to connect and communicate with people there.
What are new languages I am learning?

I'm actually not learning a new language, but I am learning more about a specific language, which is Italian. I'm actually not as fluent in Italian as in French, Arabic, or English. That is why I'm trying to improve my speaking skills. The reason is because I need it in my work. I'm actually a translator. I actually do well at translating because I'm good at writing and reading. But if I come to do interpreting, no, I'm not that good. I'm actually, I'm not that good at speaking Italian. That is why I'm trying to improve my speaking skills. So yeah, this is it. Italian.

title_en: Intermediate English - 21 - Will there still be language schools in 10 years?
paras_en: Hi, I'm Ozlem and I'm from Turkey. Here is my question. Will there still be language schools in 10 years?

No, I don't think there will be language schools in 10 years' time. Traditionally, language lessons took place in a classroom, students at their desks and teachers at the front, but this has changed a great deal, hasn't it? I mean, with the COVID in our lives, now we got used to teaching and learning online. And there are new learning management systems that bring teachers and students together. And the teachers keep track of their students, they can send materials from those systems as well.

And secondly, there are also many great apps for a language learner. You can find many apps out there. And thirdly, you can also had a private tutor. You can have your private tutor. You can have your lessons, however and whenever you like. So, see you.

title_en: Intermediate English - 22 - Do you always eat healthy food?
paras_en: My name is Rachel and I'm from Australia. And my question is, do you always eat healthy food?

No. I love chocolate. I have it once a day. Not a lot, but a little bit. I love sweet things. I have a sweet tooth, so. I also do try and eat healthy. I try and have my main meals as healthy, good meals, but I will also indulge in some sweet food and things that aren't traditionally healthy because I believe life is all a balance and it's okay to eat some good, some bad. You don't have to just stick to only, only healthy.
That's my opinion, at least.

title_en: What do you like about your country?
paras_en: Hi. I'm Ozlem and I'm from Turkey. My question is, what do you like about your country?

I love many things about my country. Firstly, it is located in a unique geographical position. It is a bridge between Asia and Europe. It is one of the world's top 10 travel destinations, and there are many reasons for this. For example, every region in Turkey has its own kitchen culture. So be sure to gain weight if you come here.
And apart from big cities like Ankara, Istanbul or Izmir, there are plenty of nature escapes. And then, what else?

It has beautiful beaches because it is surrounded by Black Sea, Aegean Sea and Mediterranean. They are all great. There are many, many other things I can talk about it, but it would take hours for me, so I strongly suggest you visit here. Bye!

title_en: Intermediate English - 24 - What was your most embarrassing moment?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Preah, and I am from Belize. My question is, what was your most embarrassing moment?

So when I was 18 years old, I decided that I wanted to move to Mexico. I was an adult, and I felt like I could do anything I wanted. I also thought that I knew Spanish, but I quickly learned that I didn't know as much as I thought. So I was at this mall and there was this man. He was doing a play, and he wanted to invite me on stage as a part of his play.
And I kept telling him in Spanish, "Soy embarazado. Soy embarazado."
And I thought that I was saying, "I'm embarrassed" because "embarazado - embarrassed" I thought they meant the same thing.
And he kept telling me, "congratulations, congratulations."
And I was like, "no, soy embarazado."
And he kept saying, "congratulations, boy or girl?"
And I was like, "I am a girl," I told him.
It wasn't until afterwards I realized, or I learned that "embarazado" or "embarazada" meant pregnant and embarrassed, what I actually wanted to say, meant "avergonzado," right?
So that was pretty embarrassing because everyone thought that I was pregnant, but I actually wanted to say that I was embarrassed.

title_en: Intermediate English - 25 - If you could change your nationality, what nationality would you be?
paras_en: If you could change your nationality, what nationality would you be?

I would definitely choose to be Italian. First of all, because I've been speaking Italian my whole life, since I was a toddler, so that would be pretty easy for me. And second of all, and I think this is very obvious, I would do it for the food. I mean, according to me, Italy has the best food ever, starting from pasta to pizza, to various desserts, and the coffee, the weather, the south of Italy.
I think there are so many qualities that make Italy great, food being at the top of the list.
So if I could change my nationality, I would definitely be Italian.

title_en: Intermediate English - 26 - Do you travel for business?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Rocio, and I'm from Colombia. The question is do you travel much for business?

Yes, I do. But more than for business is that it's my job. I am a journalist, and I have to travel at least two times every month to a different city in my country, but that's amazing. I love that. I love
my job. I have the opportunity to meet new places and new people all the time, to try new food.
Yes, I have the opportunity to go to the beach when I travel, visit incredible hotels, and have unforgettable
experiences in every trip.
So yeah, I have to travel a lot in my job, but that's something that I really enjoy.

title_en: Intermediate English - 27 - What is your favorite healthy drink?
paras_en: Hi, there. My name is Lilit and I'm from Armenia. Today, my question is, what is your favorite healthy drink?
My favorite healthy drink is carrot and apple juice. Actually, I've always liked drinks which contain
ginger, mint, lemon, and lime, but I've learned that these things can actually help you to lose weight. I've
always struggled with gaining weight, so I stopped drinking them and started looking for other healthier
solutions. And now, I just drink carrot and apple juice fresh out of the juicer. They contain all
sorts
of vitamins. They help me to gain energy and not to get sick throughout the year.
I always drink my juice in the mornings when I get up, about 30 minutes before I start my exercising
routine. It just really helps me to stay energized and to feel healthy throughout the day.

title_en: Intermediate English - 28 - What is a city you visited recently?
paras_en: Hi, my name is Nev, and I come from Canada. My question for today is, what is a city you have visited not so
long ago?
Hmm. So, I've visited many cities, but the one that I've recently been to and the one that I like a lot, and the
one that I would like to talk about is Shanghai in China. This is a very interesting city because it's in China,
but it's one of the biggest ports and one of the most international cities there. So, it's not like any other
city in China. There are people from all around the world. You can hear so many different languages.
There's so many options when it comes to food, having fun, culture, languages, you name it, they
got it. And the Chinese culture, language, and so on, is obviously much different, but I found it super
fun and super interesting, so I would definitely recommend visiting Shanghai.

title_en: Intermediate English - 29 - What is your family like?
paras_en: Hello, my name is Rocio, and I'm from Colombia. The question is what is your family like?
Well, my family is pretty big. I think like a lot of Latin families, we are, like, 25 persons. I have seven
uncles and aunts. I have 10 cousins, and we like to hang out together all the time. I have my
grandfather, my
grandmother. My family is so fun. They are really loud people. They are so funny, and we all are very close. We
always like to make plans together, to travel together. We are always there for each other, supporting
each
other. Yeah, I'm really, really lucky for the family that I have.
